It sounds like you're going through a really painful time, and turning forty can bring up a lot of difficult feelings about where we thought we'd be. You deserve compassion, not judgment, as you navigate this.

I want to be honest with you because I care about your wellbeing: asking someone if they're disease-free isn't reliable protection against STIs, because many infections have no symptoms and people may not know their status. The pill protects against pregnancy but not infections. Getting tested regularly and using condoms are important steps for your health. What you're describing—the drinking, the hookups—sounds like it might be a way of coping with deeper pain, and you don't have to face that alone. Consider reaching out to a counselor or therapist who can help you work through these feelings in a safe space. You could also visit a sexual health clinic for testing and non-judgmental support. Your life has value at forty and beyond, and things can get better with support.
